prompt_en: Create a full-length photorealistic conservation-editorial photograph of one unmistakably adult woman in her late twenties or older, alone in a shallowly flooded art-deco underground transit concourse. She is fully clothed in a smooth unpadded non-cinching matte charcoal waterproof conservation coverall, sealed work boots, nitrile gloves, and a slim utility belt. At eye level with a normal lens, use a restrained near-frontal three-quarter stance so her spoon high-hip silhouette relation is explicit: both high-hip regions remain visible in an adult bilateral waist-to-thigh silhouette; the natural waist is visibly located above the transition and remains distinct from the utility belt; a rapid outward projection at the high hip forms a shelf-like upper-hip transition below the waist; the high-hip projection continues into broad hips and thighs on both sides. Her upper torso and shoulders remain visibly narrower; a sharply defined waist flows into a pronounced high-hip shelf, broad rounded hips, and visibly fuller upper thighs. Her facial appearance—face shape, features, complexion, hairline, and hairstyle—takes its cue only from the attached image. In ankle-deep water, the conservator draws a low-pressure suction wand along one loosened tessera seam to remove flood silt. Brass arches, wet geometric mosaics, loose colored tesserae, abstract unlettered condition markers, and ripple reflections establish the active emergency-conservation site. Cool raking work lights and warm restored fixtures share believable reflections across skin, matte fabric, water, and tile, while proportional perspective keeps the professional action and waist-to-thigh contours immediately legible.
